Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.
Tags.markdownDescription:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Placements.description: The blocks that can be placed at the configured Offset. Each rule may optionally be scoped to one of this block's visual States; a rule with no State applies to the block's default (stateless) form. The first rule matching the block's current State is placed when the target cell is clear.
Placements.markdownDescription: The blocks that can be placed at the configured Offset. Each rule may optionally be scoped to one of this block's visual States; a rule with no State applies to the block's default (stateless) form. The first rule matching the block's current State is placed when the target cell is clear.

Offset.description: The block offset (relative to the ticking block) at which to place the block. For example X=0, Y=1, Z=0 places the block one cell directly above.
Offset.markdownDescription: The block offset (relative to the ticking block) at which to place the block. For example X=0, Y=1, Z=0 places the block one cell directly above.

RequireEmptyTarget.description: Whether the target cell must be empty (air) for the placement to occur. When true (the default) an obstruction causes the procedure to silently do nothing and retry on a later tick.
RequireEmptyTarget.markdownDescription: Whether the target cell must be empty (air) for the placement to occur. When true (the default) an obstruction causes the procedure to silently do nothing and retry on a later tick.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.
Tags.markdownDescription:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Parent.description:

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.
Tags.markdownDescription:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.

Type.description: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "ZOverride" to function as this type.
Type.markdownDescription: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "ZOverride" to function as this type.

Parent.description:
When set this asset will inherit properties from the named asset.

When inheriting from another ZOverrideDensityAsset most properties will simply be copied from the parent asset to this asset. In the case where both child and parent provide a field the child field will simply replace the value provided by the parent, in the case of nested structures this will apply to the fields within the structure. In some cases the field may decide to act differently, for example: by merging the parent and child fields together.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

SizeWeights.description: An array of weights which is used in conjunction with the MinSize to determine the weighted size of the flock. The first value in the array corresponds to the weight of the minimum size and each successive value to a flock larger by one. e.g. If MinSize is 2 and SizeWeights is [ 25, 75 ], there will be a 25% chance that the flock will spawn with a size of 2 and a 75% chance that the flock will spawn with a size of 3. As these are weights, they do not need to add up to 100 and their percentage is relative to the total sum.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

A collection of interaction types that should block this interaction from starting. If not set then a set of default rules will be applied based on the interaction type that theinteraction is fired with.
This is only effective when used on the root interaction of a chain.
BlockedBy.markdownDescription:
A collection of interaction types that should block this interaction from starting. If not set then a set of default rules will be applied based on the interaction type that theinteraction is fired with.
This is only effective when used on the root interaction of a chain.

Blocking.title: Set
Blocking.description:
A collection of interaction types that this interaction blocks from starting whilst running.
Defaults to an empty set (blocking nothing).
Blocking.markdownDescription:
A collection of interaction types that this interaction blocks from starting whilst running.
Defaults to an empty set (blocking nothing).

InterruptedBy.title: Set
InterruptedBy.description:

This is only effective when used on the root interaction of a chain.
InterruptedBy.markdownDescription:
A collection of interaction types that should stop this interaction while it's running.
This is only effective when used on the root interaction of a chain.

Interrupting.title: Set

ApplyEffectInteraction.title: ApplyEffectInteraction
ApplyEffectInteraction.description: Applies the given entity effect to the entity.
ApplyEffectInteraction.markdownDescription: Applies the given entity effect to the entity.

Type.description: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "ApplyEffect" to function as this type.
Type.markdownDescription: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "ApplyEffect" to function as this type.

Parent.description:
When set this asset will inherit properties from the named asset.

When inheriting from another ApplyEffectInteraction most properties will simply be copied from the parent asset to this asset. In the case where both child and parent provide a field the child field will simply replace the value provided by the parent, in the case of nested structures this will apply to the fields within the structure. In some cases the field may decide to act differently, for example: by merging the parent and child fields together.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.

Forks.title: Map of InteractionType
Forks.description:
A collection of interactions to fork into when the input associated with the interaction type is used.

For example listing a `Primary` interaction type here with interactions will allow the user to press the input tied to the `Primary` interaction type whilst holding the input used to run the current interaction to run the specified interactions. e.g. Having a shield that you can hold `Secondary` to block and whilst blocking press `Primary` to shield bash.

This does not cancel the current interaction when triggered but the `CancelOnOtherClick` check will still run and may cancel the interaction.

The existing forks will continue to run even if this interaction ends.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.

RepeatInteraction.title: RepeatInteraction
RepeatInteraction.description:
Forks from the current interaction into one or more chains that run the specified interactions.

When run this will create a new chain that will run the interactions specified in `ForkInteractions`. This will then wait until that chain completes. If the chain completes successfully it will then check the `Repeat` field to see if it needs to run again, if not then the interactions `Next` are run otherwise this repeats with the next fork. If the chain fails then any repeating is ignored and the interactions `Failed` are run instead.

SelectInteraction.title: SelectInteraction
SelectInteraction.description:
An interaction that can be used to find entities/blocks within a given area.

This runs the given `Selector` every tick this interactions runs for, the selector may change the search area over time (based on `RunTime`). e.g. to trace out an arc of a sword swing.

When an entity/block is found this interaction will run a set of interactions (as defined by `HitEntity`/`HitBlock`) per a entity/block, this will not interrupt the selector and it will continue searching until the select interaction completes.

This interaction does not wait for any forked interaction chains from `HitEntity`/`HitBlock` to complete before finishing itself.
SelectInteraction.markdownDescription:
An interaction that can be used to find entities/blocks within a given area.

This runs the given `Selector` every tick this interactions runs for, the selector may change the search area over time (based on `RunTime`). e.g. to trace out an arc of a sword swing.

When an entity/block is found this interaction will run a set of interactions (as defined by `HitEntity`/`HitBlock`) **per a entity/block**, this will not interrupt the selector and it will continue searching until the select interaction completes.

This interaction does not wait for any forked interaction chains from `HitEntity`/`HitBlock` to complete before finishing itself.

Forks.title: Map of InteractionType
Forks.description:
A collection of interactions to fork into when the input associated with the interaction type is used.

For example listing a `Primary` interaction type here with interactions will allow the user to press the input tied to the `Primary` interaction type whilst holding the input used to run the current interaction to run the specified interactions. e.g. Having a shield that you can hold `Secondary` to block and whilst blocking press `Primary` to shield bash.

This does not cancel the current interaction when triggered but the `CancelOnOtherClick` check will still run and may cancel the interaction.

The existing forks will continue to run even if this interaction ends.

HorizontalMusicContainer.title: HorizontalMusicContainer
HorizontalMusicContainer.description: A music container designed for horizontal dynamic music, where transitions go from segment to segment.
HorizontalMusicContainer.markdownDescription: A music container designed for horizontal dynamic music, where transitions go from segment to segment.

Type.description: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "Horizontal" to function as this type.
Type.markdownDescription: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "Horizontal" to function as this type.

Parent.description:
When set this asset will inherit properties from the named asset.

When inheriting from another HorizontalMusicContainer most properties will simply be copied from the parent asset to this asset. In the case where both child and parent provide a field the child field will simply replace the value provided by the parent, in the case of nested structures this will apply to the fields within the structure. In some cases the field may decide to act differently, for example: by merging the parent and child fields together.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.
Tags.markdownDescription:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.

Parent.description:

When inheriting from another AnchorPositionProviderAsset most properties will simply be copied from the parent asset to this asset. In the case where both child and parent provide a field the child field will simply replace the value provided by the parent, in the case of nested structures this will apply to the fields within the structure. In some cases the field may decide to act differently, for example: by merging the parent and child fields together.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.

Type.description: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "Union" to function as this type.
Type.markdownDescription: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "Union" to function as this type.

Parent.description:
When set this asset will inherit properties from the named asset.

When inheriting from another UnionPropDistributionAsset most properties will simply be copied from the parent asset to this asset. In the case where both child and parent provide a field the child field will simply replace the value provided by the parent, in the case of nested structures this will apply to the fields within the structure. In some cases the field may decide to act differently, for example: by merging the parent and child fields together.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.
Tags.markdownDescription:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.
Tags.markdownDescription:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.

Op.description: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "Not" to function as this type.
Op.markdownDescription: This field controls the type, it must be set to the constant value "Not" to function as this type.

Parent.description:
When set this asset will inherit properties from the named asset.

When inheriting from another NotPatternOp most properties will simply be copied from the parent asset to this asset. In the case where both child and parent provide a field the child field will simply replace the value provided by the parent, in the case of nested structures this will apply to the fields within the structure. In some cases the field may decide to act differently, for example: by merging the parent and child fields together.

IgnoreFogLimits.description: The client has a default minimum AND maximum for "FogFar". Toggling this on will allow your FogDistance[1] to bypass those limits.
IgnoreFogLimits.markdownDescription: The client has a default minimum AND maximum for "FogFar". Toggling this on will allow your FogDistance[1] to bypass those limits.

EffectiveViewDistanceMultiplier.description: The client's default cap for FogDistance[1] (aka FogFar) is the effective view distance, meaning the farthest viewable chunk. This value (defaults 1.0) multiplies that cap. For example with high fog density, you can afford a fog multiplier of 1.3 as the cutoff of unloaded chunks may still be hidden.
EffectiveViewDistanceMultiplier.markdownDescription: The client's default cap for FogDistance[1] (aka FogFar) is the effective view distance, meaning the farthest viewable chunk. This value (defaults 1.0) multiplies that cap. For example with high fog density, you can afford a fog multiplier of 1.3 as the cutoff of unloaded chunks may still be hidden.

FogHeightCameraFixed.description: By default, the client has e^(-FogHeightFalloff * ~Camera.Y) height-based fog. This adds significant fog near Camera.Y = 0. By setting this value (between 0.0 and 1.0), the Exp function is bypassed and there will be a fixed fog for height in the fog shader.
FogHeightCameraFixed.markdownDescription: By default, the client has e^(-FogHeightFalloff * ~Camera.Y) height-based fog. This adds significant fog near Camera.Y = 0. By setting this value (between 0.0 and 1.0), the Exp function is bypassed and there will be a fixed fog for height in the fog shader.

FogHeightCameraOffset.description: By default, the client has e^(-FogHeightFalloff * ~Camera.Y) height-based fog. This adds significant fog near Camera.Y = 0. The FogHeightCameraOffset is added to the Camera.Y.
FogHeightCameraOffset.markdownDescription: By default, the client has e^(-FogHeightFalloff * ~Camera.Y) height-based fog. This adds significant fog near Camera.Y = 0. The FogHeightCameraOffset is added to the Camera.Y.

Tags.title: Map
Tags.description:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.

Tags.title: Map

Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a Material tag with the values Solid and Stone, And another single tag Ore.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with Material and Ore the end result would be the following list of tags: Ore, Material, Solid, Stone, Material=Solid and Material=Stone.
